dedupe_keys.name: u s doe solar decathlon now buildingsnext student design competition

description: The U.S. Department of Energy BuildingsNEXT Student Design Competition, formerly the Solar Decathlon, is a collegiate competition in which student teams design, and in the Build Challenge also construct, high-performance buildings that use energy efficiently and affordably and are powered by renewables. The first Build Challenge was held in 2002 and then every two years from 2005 to 2023; the Race to Zero competition joined in 2019 as the one- to two-semester Design Challenge, held each year from 2019 to 2024. Teams have studied the design of apartments, houses, schools and offices, and the competition has spread to international events. Coverage: United States, with international spin-off events in many regions. Access: the DOE about page and the competition website with past event pages. Licence: U.S. government work; free. Caveats: solardecathlon.gov failed TLS checks here, so facts come from the DOE page; team design documents and measured house performance vary by year. Simulation uses are as a source of documented net-zero house designs and measured competition performance for model testing and education. Related records: the NIST Net-Zero Energy Residential Test Facility.

name: U.S. DOE Solar Decathlon (now BuildingsNEXT Student Design Competition)
outcomes: Since 2002 the competition has involved more than 900 collegiate teams and more than 25,000 participants from over 40 countries, with Build Challenges in 2002 and biennially from 2005 to 2023 and annual Design Challenges from 2019 to 2024, and has expanded through more than 15 international events in Europe, China, Latin America, Africa, India and the Middle East.
resources_used: Team-designed and built high-performance houses and buildings
